objective: Help people understand nuclear projects, compare public evidence, and see what remains unknown across the nuclear lifecycle.

workflow.title: Collect
workflow.detail: Gather public records from approved sources and record when each source was checked.
workflow.caveat: The collection workflow is configured for daily checks. A schedule does not prove a recent successful run.

workflow.title: Keep the original
workflow.detail: Preserve imported records in local SQLite, with original JSON snapshots and their source dates.
workflow.caveat: Scheduled collection receipts remain in Git. Local imports are separate; automatic collection into SQLite is not connected.

workflow.title: Review the evidence
workflow.detail: Check the source, dates, and facility match. Keep unknowns and conflicts visible.
workflow.caveat: Human review is required before publication. Google Sheets and the reviewed workbook remain the authoring layer.

workflow.title: Publish a snapshot
workflow.detail: Validate the reviewed release and generate the static website and public downloads.
workflow.caveat: Automatic publication of new source claims is not connected. Existing public releases remain dated.

workflow.title: Explore the lifecycle
workflow.detail: Use Map and Table to find records and inspect the public evidence behind them.
workflow.caveat: All seven stages contain records. Coverage remains uneven and primarily U.S.; an empty result is not a known zero.

storage.title: Local SQLite collection archive
storage.detail: Imported source records, collection metadata, and citations are stored locally. Original JSON snapshots sit beside the database, with dated SQLite backups. This archive does not publish to the website.

storage.title: Git retains collection receipts
storage.detail: The existing scheduled collection workflow stores retrieval receipts, review candidates, and evidence history in Git. It is not automatically connected to the local SQLite archive.

storage.title: Reviewed workbook and static releases
storage.detail: Google Sheets and the reviewed workbook remain the authoring layer. Approved release JSON generates the public website and downloads. Visitors do not query SQLite or Google Sheets.

storage.title: Retention and recovery beyond this computer
storage.detail: Local database backups exist. An off-device backup destination, per-source raw-file retention, and unattended collection into SQLite remain to be defined. Existing permitted Actions artifacts retain their configured 90-day lifetime.
storage.location: No off-device SQLite backup is configured

decisions.title: History and queries
decisions.question: Do we only serve current snapshots, or need reliable queries across years of records?
decisions.acceptance: Measure daily records, growth, and the historical queries a real user needs.

decisions.title: Retention and recovery
decisions.question: Which raw records can we retain, for how long, and how do we restore them?
decisions.acceptance: Approve per-source retention, export an archive, and prove a hash-checked restore.

decisions.title: Publication authority
decisions.question: Who can approve evidence, and what may deterministic code publish?
decisions.acceptance: Keep human review; test permissions, conflicts, rollback, and failure without an AI reviewer.

decisions.title: Time and identity
decisions.question: How do we reconcile dates and entities without inventing precision?
decisions.acceptance: Define stable IDs, preserve original dates, and test offset and daylight-saving conversions.

ui.title: Discover
ui.detail: Lifecycle tabs come first. A persona lens sets a starting view; search, technology, evidence strength, and location precision narrow it. Sources are available from the health trigger.

ui.title: Explore
ui.detail: Map and Table share records and selection. Desktop has a layer rail and inspector; mobile uses drawers and a full-height evidence sheet.

ui.title: Verify
ui.detail: The inspector exposes cited records, verification dates, contractual support, and location precision. Users can download public data or open the full project page.

ui.title: Understand missing coverage
ui.detail: Replace empty-map warnings with a Coverage Workspace showing relevant sources, blockers, and the next publication milestone. Do not turn missing coverage into a count of zero.

rules.title: Source authority has limits
rules.detail: A license proves a regulatory action, not project profitability. Company statements remain company claims. Third-party trackers help discover evidence; they do not replace it.

rules.title: Unknown stays unknown
rules.detail: Do not infer private prices, supplier lead times, available fuel, or spare spent fuel capacity. Separate contracted capacity from options and preliminary plans.

rules.title: Keep dates distinct
rules.detail: A source publication date, an effective date, and a retrieval time answer different questions. Preserve date-only values and original periods; UTC instants retain their Z suffix.

rules.title: Show how fresh the evidence is
rules.detail: Sources publish on different schedules. Checking a source today does not make its older records current. Collection failures must remain visible.

rules.title: Corrections remain visible
rules.detail: Retain evidence history and cite the replacement. Source outages must not erase approved facts. Conflicts and ambiguous entity matches require a human decision.

rules.title: People approve factual changes
rules.detail: A successful download or an AI summary does not authorize publication. Human review checks the supporting evidence and resolves ambiguous matches before a new release.

questions: Who is buying power from whom?
How binding is the commitment?
What capacity and target dates are actually supported?
projects.next: The current Projects dataset covers announced fission deals with named large-load buyers or developers. It is not an inventory of every planned reactor.

questions: Which facilities provide each step of the fuel cycle?
Which fuel types do planned reactors require?
Which publicly documented constraints affect supply?
fuel-supply.next: Facility listings do not establish available supply, private contracts, or supplier lead times.

questions: Which applications and permits have been filed?
Which approvals and construction milestones are complete?
What is the next documented decision or deadline?
build-license.next: Selected licensing records are published. Applications, approvals, and construction milestones are not comprehensively tracked.

questions: Which reactors report operating power?
How has reported output changed?
What official records explain an outage or event?
operations.next: The NRC snapshot includes operating status and oversight records. Live output and complete generation histories are not available here.

questions: Where are licensed spent fuel storage sites?
What inventory and storage systems are documented?
What do licenses explicitly allow?
spent-fuel.next: Storage licensing records are published. Inventory and remaining capacity are not inferred.

questions: Which facilities handle which waste classes?
What is each facility's regulatory status?
Which documented acceptance conditions apply?
waste-disposal.next: Selected public disposal records are included. Waste acceptance rules and service areas need source-specific interpretation.

questions: Which sites are in each decommissioning phase?
What milestones and target dates are documented?
What obligations remain for cleanup and stored fuel?
decommissioning.next: Public status and strategy records are included. Detailed costs, schedules, and historical milestones remain incomplete.

releaseChecks: Reproduce every material claim from a cited source and locator.
Keep Map and Table record IDs identical under every filter.
Show location precision, source dates, and collection failures without implying certainty.
Pass mobile, keyboard, contrast, static-export, and public-download tests.
Before a storage cutover, reconcile shadow runs and restore archived records.
Before automatic publication, approve each source, adapter version, and claim type explicitly.
nonGoals: No private-price or supplier-capacity estimates presented as facts.
No universal readiness, safety, or investment score.
No claim of complete global or lifecycle coverage.
No AI-authorized publication of factual changes.
rubric: Announced intent, memorandum, or nonbinding letter
Funded development or feasibility work without binding offtake
Signed power purchase or definitive agreement
Binding agreement plus physical or regulatory progress
Dead, lapsed, or superseded, retained as history

audiences.title: Researchers and analysts
audiences.detail: Find facilities and projects, compare their public records, and trace claims to original sources.

audiences.title: Developers, buyers, and suppliers
audiences.detail: Explore documented projects, licensing activity, and fuel-cycle facilities. Private commercial availability remains unknown.

audiences.title: Communities and journalists
audiences.detail: Understand what is documented about a site, its lifecycle, and its public regulatory record.

audiences.title: Industry professionals
audiences.detail: Follow related facilities and evidence across operations, spent fuel, waste, and decommissioning.
